title: YG SHADER
description: YG SHADER brings a vivid, glowing Vibrant Visuals atmosphere to Minecraft Bedrock — pink sun rays in cherry blossom groves, green rays in forests, dramatic purple-violet sunsets, and a glowing violet mood in caves.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: YG SHADER is an original Vibrant Visuals atmosphere pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition, built from the ground up to turn ordinary daylight and night cycles into something vivid, glowing and a little dreamlike. It doesn't touch any block models or vanilla textures — instead it rewrites how light, sky and fog behave, using Minecraft's own Vibrant Visuals (deferred lighting) system. COLOR-CODED SUN RAYS BY BIOME Every biome now has its own light-shaft color. Walk into a cherry blossom grove and the sunlight filtering through the petals glows a soft, dreamy pink. Step into a forest and the same light turns a rich, leafy green as it filters through the canopy. Jungles carry a deep humid green haze, deserts a warm dusty gold, swamps a murky olive-green, and snowy biomes a pale icy blue. Each mood is tuned individually through the biome's own fog settings, so the light always feels like it belongs to the place you're standing in. DRAMATIC, PURPLE-TINTED SKIES Sunrise and sunset no longer fade through plain orange. The sky now sweeps from warm gold into rose-pink and then deep violet-magenta before settling into night, giving every dawn and dusk a cinematic, almost aurora-like quality. Midday skies are a clean, saturated blue, and nights shift into a deep indigo-violet rather than flat black, with a cooler, slightly purple moonlight. STRONGER GLOW EVERYWHERE Light sources are noticeably brighter and more saturated: torches, lanterns, campfires, glowstone, sea lanterns, beacons, amethyst clusters, end rods and portals all glow harder and spill more color onto nearby blocks. Caves get their own atmosphere too — Lush Caves and Dripstone Caves now carry a glowing violet-purple haze, giving underground exploration a mysterious, otherworldly feel instead of flat grey stone lighting. RICHER COLOR GRADING On top of the sky and lighting changes, YG SHADER applies its own color grading pass — boosted saturation across highlights, midtones and shadows, a touch more contrast, and a slightly raised exposure — so colors read as vivid and alive rather than washed out, without ever tipping into neon or unnatural territory. WHAT THIS PACK DOES NOT DO To set expectations correctly: YG SHADER works entirely through Minecraft's documented Vibrant Visuals resource-pack system (sky, fog, lighting, color grading, water). It cannot create custom cloud shapes, floating glowing objects, or any effect that isn't part of that system — those would need a completely different kind of mod. What it changes is color, light and atmosphere, not geometry. REQUIREMENTS YG SHADER requires a Minecraft Bedrock version with Vibrant Visuals support, with Vibrant Visuals turned on in both Video settings and your world's settings. Without that toggle enabled, none of the pack's sky, lighting or fog changes will appear, so please double-check it's on if things don't look different after importing. YG SHADER is built entirely from original, self-authored settings and artwork — no files, textures or code from any other shader or resource pack are used. Enjoy the glow! Credits YG SHADER : created and tuned entirely by yogamerzyt Minecraft : Mojang Studios / Microsoft. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Mojang or Microsoft.

title: BASE VISUALS
description: BASE VISUALS is a lighting and atmosphere pack for Vibrant Visuals. It adds biome-coloured sun rays, golden-lavender sunsets, moonlit nights, glowing lanterns, water caustics and a vivid Nether and End. By Baku_Studio.

fullDescription: BASE VISUALS: A Beautiful Base for Your Minecraft World BASE VISUALS is a lighting and atmosphere pack for Minecraft Bedrock, built for Vibrant Visuals. It keeps the blocks, textures and feel of classic Minecraft and changes only the light around them. Instead of one grey-white light for the whole world, every biome gets its own colour of sunlight, haze, sky and water. Step into a cherry grove and the rays turn soft pink. Walk into a jungle and the light becomes deep emerald. Every place feels different. What You Get Biome-coloured sun rays. The pack tints the volumetric fog that carries the light shafts, so the rays take the colour of the biome around you. It covers all 89 biomes with 39 hand-tuned light themes, including caves, oceans and the other dimensions. A few examples: Cherry Grove: rose-pink rays with a dreamy glow Jungle and Bamboo Jungle: emerald and lime-green shafts Birch and Forest: warm champagne-gold light Dark Forest: golden light cutting through dark canopies Autumn Forest: fiery orange rays over vivid red and orange leaves Taiga: cool mint-teal light Snowy Biomes: icy blue rays Desert, Savanna and Badlands: amber, orange and terracotta light Oceans: aqua, turquoise and deep blue Mushroom Fields: violet-magenta haze Golden-lavender sunsets and sunrises. At dusk and dawn the sky blends from soft lavender at the top to peach and rose near the horizon. The sunlight turns golden-orange, then deepens toward pink as the sun sinks. Rays streaming through trees at this hour are the pack's signature look. Moonlit nights. Night skies are a deep indigo-violet with soft purple-white moonlight and a bright glow around the moon. Warm, coloured local lights. Torches, lanterns, campfires, candles, glowstone, lava and other light sources cast their own coloured light on nearby blocks. Soul torches glow blue, copper torches glow green, and amethyst glows violet. Lantern-lit paths at night are one of the pack's best moments. Water with caustics. Shallow water shows animated, net-like caustic patterns on the floor, and water is tuned to look clean and turquoise, with a subtle tint from each biome. The caustics texture was created from scratch for this pack. Moody rain. During rain the haze turns a cool blue-grey, only lightly tinted by the biome, so storms feel wet and atmospheric. A vivid End. The End has a deep violet sky, a magenta glow near the horizon and a soft lavender beam of light, with its own colour grading. A redesigned Nether. Nether wastes, Crimson Forest, Warped Forest, Soul Sand Valley and Basalt Deltas each have their own sky, light colour and ambient glow, wrapped in thick, rich haze. Soft shadows and rich colour. Soft-edged shadows and a colour-grading pass add depth, contrast and saturation without crushing shadows or blowing out highlights. Two Versions BASE VISUALS: the main pack, with rich, clearly visible colour. BASE VISUALS (Soft): the same idea with gentler rays, for a more natural look. How to Use It Import the .mcpack file by tapping or double-clicking it. Do not unzip it into a folder. Go to Settings, then Global Resources, and activate BASE VISUALS. Turn on Vibrant Visuals in Video Settings. For the best rays, explore at sunrise or sunset, near trees, hills or clouds where light is broken up. Tips Use only one Vibrant Visuals pack at a time to avoid conflicts. If the effect feels too strong, switch to the Soft version. Light shafts are strongest when the sun is low and something casts shadows. Cloud shape and softness depend on the game's own Vibrant Visuals settings and your device, not on this pack. Compatibility Built for Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.120 and newer, with Vibrant Visuals enabled. It needs a device that supports Vibrant Visuals. Performance depends on your hardware and render distance. Originality All configuration files, colour values, the caustics texture and the pack icon in this pack were made from scratch. It uses no textures, files or assets from other packs. Not affiliated: This is an unofficial community creation. It is not made by, endorsed by, or associated with Mojang Studios or Microsoft. Minecraft is a trademark of Mojang Studios. Usage: Free for personal play and content creation. Please credit Baku_Studio, and do not re-upload or sell this pack as your own work.

title: ABHU VISUALS
description: ABHU VISUALS recolours Minecraft's Vibrant Visuals sunlight, moonlight and haze for each biome, so light shafts glow pink, green, blue or gold depending on where you stand. Original work by GURJAR.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: ABHU VISUALS is a Vibrant Visuals pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition that gives every biome its own colour of light. Walk into a cherry grove at sunrise and the beams drifting through the blossoms glow soft pink. Step into a forest and the same sunlight turns fresh emerald. Cross into a snowy taiga and the rays cool to a silvery blue, while deserts and savannas burn with warm amber. The pack never replaces your textures or changes gameplay. It simply repaints the atmosphere, so your world feels like a different place wherever you travel. The look is built on three ideas. First, directional lighting: the sun and moon each carry a biome-specific tint, and that tint reaches blocks, leaves, water surfaces and the sky. Second, volumetric fog: every featured biome has a thin, coloured haze that catches the light and turns it into visible shafts between trunks, hills and clouds. Third, a gentle day and night cycle: sunrise and sunset blend each tint toward a warm glow, and nights switch to a cool moonlit palette that matches the biome you are standing in. Featured biomes include Cherry Grove, Forest, Flower Forest, Birch Forest, Plains, Sunflower Plains, Taiga, Old Growth Taiga, Snowy Taiga, Snowy Plains, Windswept Hills, Jungle, Bamboo Jungle, Savanna and Desert. Every other biome keeps its normal Mojang look, but its sunlight is still gently re-tinted so swamps, mushroom fields, pale gardens, ice spikes, badlands and the like feel consistent with the rest of the pack. Everything in ABHU VISUALS is original. The pack contains no copied shaders, textures or code. It is made entirely from the official Vibrant Visuals data files that Minecraft already supports, namely lighting, fog and client biome definitions, and all colour values were chosen by hand for this project. Light intensity follows the current vanilla scale, so exposure, shadows and the day cycle stay balanced and nothing looks blown out. Because it relies on official data files, no mods, launchers, OptiFine or Iris are needed. It works in the standard Bedrock app on any device that supports Vibrant Visuals. Performance depends on your hardware, but the pack adds no extra textures and only a few small configuration files, so it asks for very little beyond what Vibrant Visuals already uses. How to install: open the downloaded file with Minecraft so it imports automatically, go to Settings, then Global Resources, and activate ABHU VISUALS. Next open Settings, then Video, and switch Vibrant Visuals on. Load a world, and for the best first impression travel to a cherry grove or a forest around sunrise or sunset, when light shafts are strongest. Compatibility: designed for Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.100 and newer, including the 26.x releases. Older versions do not support the Vibrant Visuals pack format, and Vibrant Visuals itself must be enabled or you will see no difference. The Nether and the End are intentionally left untouched so their carefully tuned vanilla atmospheres are preserved. Two strengths are included. The standard edition aims for a natural, balanced look, while the Strong edition pushes colour, haze and beam density for a more dramatic, screenshot-style result. A small Test pack is also provided so you can confirm that your device loads Vibrant Visuals packs correctly before judging the look. Credits: created and designed by GURJAR. Minecraft and Vibrant Visuals belong to Mojang Studios and Microsoft. This pack is an independent fan-made creation and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by Mojang or Microsoft. Feel free to share it, but please keep the credit to GURJAR when you do. Feature list Biome-specific sun and moon colours with a warm blend at sunrise and sunset Coloured volumetric haze that turns sunlight into visible light shafts 15 featured biomes with their own palette, remaining Overworld biomes gently re-tinted Light intensity on the current vanilla scale, so exposure and shadows stay balanced Nether and End left untouched Three files: Standard, Strong (more colour and haze) and a Test pack for checking that packs load 100% original configuration, no copied shaders, textures or code No mods, launchers, OptiFine or Iris required Installation Open the downloaded .mcpack file with Minecraft so it imports itself. Settings > Global Resources > activate ABHU VISUALS (it must appear under Active). Settings > Video > turn Vibrant Visuals on. Load a world and look toward the sun in a cherry grove or forest at sunrise or sunset. If you copy the files by hand, the pack folder must contain manifest.json directly inside it (not inside another folder). Requirements and compatibility Minecraft Bedrock Edition 1.21.100 or newer, including the 26.x versions A device that supports Vibrant Visuals Not for Java Edition Known limitations Vibrant Visuals must be enabled, otherwise the pack has no visible effect. This pack uses Minecraft's official data files, so it cannot match the look of third-party shader packs; it recolours the light and haze Vibrant Visuals already renders. The strongest beams appear near sunrise and sunset and through trees or hills; rain and thunderstorms mute them. The pack replaces the client definition of its 19 featured biome IDs. Those biomes keep default grass and foliage tint and default biome music. If anything looks off, try the Standard edition and note which biome. Results may need small colour tuning per device and version. Credits and legal Created and designed by GURJAR. Minecraft and Vibrant Visuals are trademarks of Mojang Studios and Microsoft. This pack is an independent, fan-made creation and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by Mojang or Microsoft. You may share the pack, but please keep the credit to GURJAR. title: No Fog - All Biomes
description: Removes Minecraft's fog - water, air, weather, lava and powder snow - in every biome. Four levels, one of which keeps the Nether's fog. Resource pack only, no behaviour pack. Works with Vibrant Visuals. Put it at the top of your active list.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: Removes Minecraft's fog - water, air, weather, lava and powder snow - in every biome. Four levels Pick one from the dropdown in the pack settings. They are listed in this order, and the last one is selected automatically, so most players never need to open the dropdown at all. Water only. All, Nether keeps fog. All except lava. All. This is the recommended one and the default. What changes Water. Vanilla fog ends at 60 blocks. Removed, so you can see across the sea floor. Lava. Vanilla fog ends at 0.64 blocks. Removed, so you can look at a distant wall while swimming in a lava sea. Weather. Vanilla fog runs from 23 to 70 percent of your render distance. Removed, so rain no longer closes in your view. Air. The distance haze is removed. Powder snow. Vanilla fog ends 2 blocks ahead. Removed. Nether. Vanilla air fog there is only 15 to 20 blocks, so this is the biggest change of all. Choose "All, Nether keeps fog" if you want to keep that closed-in atmosphere. Vibrant Visuals Tested with Vibrant Visuals enabled. Water, lava and the Nether are cleared exactly the same as without it. One thing this pack cannot touch: Vibrant Visuals has its own volumetric fog, the hazy light shafts around light sources. That is a separate system from biome fog, so no resource pack can change it. It has its own toggle in the video settings if you don't want it. Vibrant Visuals also uses its own render distance slider, so how far you can see is capped by that rather than by this pack. About the comparison screenshots Vanilla water fog is not constant. Right after you dive it sits at about 15 blocks, then it opens up over roughly 30 seconds and settles at 60. The before shots on this page were taken after it had fully settled. That is the fairest comparison, not the murkiest possible frame. Important: put this pack at the top of your active list This pack replaces the biome fog definitions, and only the topmost pack that does so is used. If another pack sits above this one, this one does nothing. Notes Resource pack only. No behaviour pack, no scripts, no commands. Achievements are unaffected. Fog is not render distance. You still only see as far as your render distance setting allows. On a server, that server's render distance still applies. Servers that use the /fog command will override this pack, because the command layer takes priority. Removing weather fog is a real visibility advantage in PvP. Check your server or tournament rules. This is not an X-ray. Block rendering is untouched, so hidden blocks stay hidden. Lava looks completely normal from the outside and only turns clear once the camera is inside it. Per-biome water colours are preserved. All 94 vanilla biome entries are kept as they are and only the fog reference is changed, so swamp water is still swamp water. All four levels work the same on every device, including phones and tablets. The pack name and description are translated into all 29 languages Minecraft offers, so it shows in your own language in game. 67 files, 31 KB. No textures, just fog definitions. Installation Download the .mcpack and open it. Enable it under Global Resources in settings. Move it to the top of the list and pick a level from the dropdown. Development notes Four things that took the longest to get right, in case they help other pack makers. Your own namespace. Fog definitions in the minecraft: namespace cannot be overridden from a resource pack. A file that reuses a vanilla fog identifier is simply ignored. This pack defines its own fog, kentotukun:no_fog, points every biome's fog_identifier at it, and sets remove_all_prior_fog to true. Two biome formats. Biomes are now defined in two places: the older biomes_client.json and newer per-biome files in the biomes folder. Some biomes, including the deep dark, lush caves, the pale garden and every mutated variant, exist only in the newer format. Replacing only the older file leaves fog in those biomes. fog_start. Fog density is calculated between fog_start and fog_end. A fog_start of 0 leaves a faint tint at every distance. Moving fog_start beyond the visible range is what removes fog completely. memory_tier. Subpacks with different memory tiers are picked by device memory, so a low-memory phone may not get the level you meant as the default. Giving every subpack the same tier makes the game pick the last one in the list on every device. title: AAUKA VISUALS
description: Removes all lava, water, snow, weather fog and nether particles. Supports A&S and Vibrant Visuals.

fullDescription: AAUKA VISUALS is a Vibrant Visuals pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition that gives every biome its own colour of light. Walk into a cherry grove at sunrise and the beams drifting through the blossoms glow soft pink. Step into a forest and the same sunlight turns fresh emerald. Cross into a snowy taiga and the rays cool to a silvery blue, while deserts and savannas burn with warm amber. The pack never replaces your textures or changes gameplay. It simply repaints the atmosphere, so your world feels like a different place wherever you travel. The look is built on three ideas. First, directional lighting: the sun and moon each carry a biome-specific tint, and that tint reaches blocks, leaves, water surfaces and the sky. Second, volumetric fog: every featured biome has a thin, coloured haze that catches the light and turns it into visible shafts between trunks, hills and clouds. Third, a gentle day and night cycle: sunrise and sunset blend each tint toward a warm glow, and nights switch to a cool moonlit palette that matches the biome you are standing in. Featured biomes include Cherry Grove, Forest, Flower Forest, Birch Forest, Plains, Sunflower Plains, Taiga, Old Growth Taiga, Snowy Taiga, Snowy Plains, Windswept Hills, Jungle, Bamboo Jungle, Savanna and Desert. Every other biome keeps its normal Mojang look, but its sunlight is still gently re-tinted so swamps, mushroom fields, pale gardens, ice spikes, badlands and the like feel consistent with the rest of the pack. Everything in AAUKA VISUALS is original. The pack contains no copied shaders, textures or code. It is made entirely from the official Vibrant Visuals data files that Minecraft already supports, namely lighting, fog and client biome definitions, and all colour values were chosen by hand for this project. Light intensity follows the current vanilla scale, so exposure, shadows and the day cycle stay balanced and nothing looks blown out. Because it relies on official data files, no mods, launchers, OptiFine or Iris are needed. It works in the standard Bedrock app on any device that supports Vibrant Visuals. Performance depends on your hardware, but the pack adds no extra textures and only a few small configuration files, so it asks for very little beyond what Vibrant Visuals already uses. How to install: open the downloaded file with Minecraft so it imports automatically, go to Settings, then Global Resources, and activate AAUKA VISUALS. Next open Settings, then Video, and switch Vibrant Visuals on. Load a world, and for the best first impression travel to a cherry grove or a forest around sunrise or sunset, when light shafts are strongest. Compatibility: designed for Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.120 and newer, including the 26.x releases. Older versions do not support the Vibrant Visuals pack format, and Vibrant Visuals itself must be enabled or you will see no difference. The Nether and the End are intentionally left untouched so their carefully tuned vanilla atmospheres are preserved. A Safe edition is included for anyone who wants the lowest possible risk. It only re-tints sunlight and moonlight and does not touch any biome definitions, so grass, water, music and sounds are guaranteed to stay exactly as Mojang made them. The full edition adds coloured volumetric haze for the featured biomes and is the one that produces the strongest, most colourful beams. Credits: created and designed by GURJAR. Minecraft and Vibrant Visuals belong to Mojang Studios and Microsoft. This pack is an independent fan-made creation and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by Mojang or Microsoft. Feel free to share it, but please keep the credit to GURJAR when you do. Feature list Biome-specific sun and moon colours with a warm blend at sunrise and sunset Coloured volumetric haze that turns sunlight into visible light shafts 15 featured biomes with their own palette, remaining Overworld biomes gently re-tinted Light intensity on the current vanilla scale, so exposure and shadows stay balanced Nether and End left untouched Two editions: Full (coloured haze) and Safe (tinted light only) 100% original configuration, no copied shaders, textures or code No mods, launchers, OptiFine or Iris required Installation Open the downloaded .mcpack file with Minecraft so it imports itself. Settings > Global Resources > activate AAUKA VISUALS. Settings > Video > turn Vibrant Visuals on. Load a world and look toward the sun in a cherry grove or forest at sunrise or sunset. If you copy the files by hand, the pack folder must contain manifest.json directly inside it (not inside another folder). Requirements and compatibility Minecraft Bedrock Edition 1.21.120 or newer, including the 26.x versions A device that supports Vibrant Visuals Not for Java Edition Known limitations Vibrant Visuals must be enabled, otherwise the pack has no visible effect. The strongest beams appear near sunrise and sunset and through trees or hills; rain and thunderstorms mute them. The Full edition replaces the client definition of its 19 featured biome IDs. Those biomes keep default grass and foliage tint and default biome music. If anything looks off, use the Safe edition. Results may need small colour tuning per device and version. fullDescription: CLASSIC VISUALS: Classic Minecraft, Beautiful Light CLASSIC VISUALS is a lighting and atmosphere pack for Minecraft Bedrock, built for Vibrant Visuals. It keeps the blocks, textures and feel of classic Minecraft and changes only the light around them. Instead of one grey-white light for the whole world, every biome gets its own colour of sunlight, haze, sky and water. Step into a cherry grove and the rays turn soft pink. Walk into a jungle and the light becomes deep emerald. Every biome feels like a different place. What You Get Biome-coloured sun rays. The pack tints the volumetric fog that carries the light shafts, so the rays take the colour of the biome around you. It covers all 89 biomes with 39 hand-tuned light themes, including caves, oceans and the other dimensions. A few examples: Cherry Grove: rose-pink rays with a dreamy glow Jungle and Bamboo Jungle: emerald and lime-green shafts Birch and Forest: warm champagne-gold light Dark Forest: golden light cutting through dark canopies Autumn Forest: fiery orange rays Taiga: cool mint-teal light Snowy Biomes: icy blue rays Desert, Savanna and Badlands: amber, orange and terracotta light Oceans: aqua, turquoise and deep blue Mushroom Fields: violet-magenta haze Pink sunsets and sunrises. At dusk and dawn the sky blends from dusky violet at the top to rose-pink around the sun. The sunlight itself turns pink, so the rays at that time of day glow pink too. This is the best moment to look for light shafts. Moody rain. During rain the haze turns a cool blue-grey, only lightly tinted by the biome, so storms feel wet and atmospheric. Deep, glowing nights. Night skies are a rich navy-indigo with soft blue moonlight. Lanterns, torches and glow berries stand out warmly against the dark. A dramatic End. The End has a magenta-purple haze with a golden-orange beam of light cutting through it, plus its own colour grading. A redesigned Nether. Nether wastes, Crimson Forest, Warped Forest, Soul Sand Valley and Basalt Deltas each have their own sky, light colour and ambient glow. Matching water and colour. Water surfaces are tuned to each biome. A gentle colour-grading pass adds a little contrast and saturation without crushing shadows or blowing out highlights. Two Versions CLASSIC VISUALS: the main pack, with rich, clearly visible colour. CLASSIC VISUALS (Soft): the same idea with gentler rays, for a more natural look. How to Use It Import the .mcpack file by tapping or double-clicking it. Go to Settings, then Global Resources, and activate CLASSIC VISUALS. Turn on Vibrant Visuals in Video Settings. For the best rays, explore at sunrise or sunset, near trees, hills or clouds where light is broken up. Tips Use only one Vibrant Visuals pack at a time to avoid conflicts. If the effect feels too strong, switch to the Soft version. Light shafts are strongest when the sun is low and something casts shadows. Compatibility Built for Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.120 and newer, with Vibrant Visuals enabled. It needs a device that supports Vibrant Visuals. Performance depends on your hardware and render distance. Originality All configuration files, colour values and the pack icon in this pack were made from scratch. It uses no textures, files or assets from other packs. Creator and Credits Pack name: CLASSIC VISUALS Author / Creator: Baku_Studio Version: 1.1.0 Platform: Minecraft Bedrock Edition (Vibrant Visuals) Minimum engine version: 1.21.120 Credits: Concept, direction and reference screenshots by Baku_Studio. Not affiliated: This is an unofficial community creation. It is not made by, endorsed by, or associated with Mojang Studios or Microsoft. Minecraft is a trademark of Mojang Studios. Usage: Free for personal play and content creation. Please credit Baku_Studio, and do not re-upload or sell this pack as your own work.

fullDescription: Original work by : PngBR JUST A DREAM . Alpha Dreams is a nostalgic Minecraft Bedrock resource pack inspired by the early days of Minecraft, Alpha, Beta and the classic Pocket Edition era. The project began as Old Craft, but evolved far beyond its original concept. Alpha Dreams aims to recreate the atmosphere, colors, textures and visual identity of old Minecraft while keeping the pack playable on modern Bedrock versions. ✦ What is Alpha Dreams? Alpha Dreams is more than just an old-style texture pack. The goal is to make modern Minecraft feel like a forgotten version of the game, combining classic textures, old Pocket Edition aesthetics, retro interfaces, nostalgic sounds and other details inspired by Minecraft's early history. The pack currently includes two different visual experiences: Alpha Textures A visual style inspired by Minecraft's early Alpha era. This subpack focuses on the simpler, rougher and more experimental appearance of early Minecraft, with classic-looking textures, old colors and a more primitive atmosphere. Beta Textures A separate visual style inspired by Minecraft Beta and the classic Pocket Edition era. Beta Textures features its own block textures, color maps, menu panoramas and other visual differences, creating a more colorful and recognizable old-school Pocket Edition feeling. Switching between Alpha and Beta changes more than a few textures. Each subpack is designed to represent a different period of Minecraft's visual history. ✦ Features • Alpha-inspired textures • Beta/Pocket Edition-inspired textures • Alpha and Beta subpacks • Old-style touchscreen controls • Retro HUD elements • Classic-looking hotbar and interface elements • Old-style menu presentation • Animated title fade-in • Animated splash text • Custom Alpha Dreams logo • Custom Minecraft-style panoramas • Alternate Beta panoramas • Legacy-inspired block textures • Legacy-inspired item textures • Classic End-related textures • Old-style End Portal Frame • Custom moon phases • Updated painting textures • Custom pumpkin overlay • Hundreds of splash texts • Retro-inspired food and item textures • Custom grass and foliage color maps • Different visual variations between Alpha and Beta • Support for modern Bedrock versions ✦ A Different Kind of Nostalgia Alpha Dreams does not try to recreate one specific Minecraft version perfectly. Instead, it explores the feeling of remembering Minecraft from years ago. Alpha represents the early, experimental days. Beta represents the colorful era that many players experienced through early Minecraft and Pocket Edition. The result is a mixture of old textures, modern Minecraft and memories from different periods of the game's history. ✦ Development Alpha Dreams is an evolving project. The current 1.0.4 release marks the transition from Days At The Origins into the Alpha Dreams era and introduces the Alpha and Beta subpack system, expanded legacy textures, retro controls, new UI elements, custom panoramas and many other changes. More content is planned for future updates, including additional legacy models, sounds, interface elements and a Modern subpack designed to reinterpret newer Minecraft content through the Alpha Dreams aesthetic. ✦ Credits Created by PngBR. Alpha Dreams is a fan-made Minecraft Bedrock resource pack created for nostalgic purposes. Minecraft is owned by Mojang Studios and Microsoft.

title: X RAY + Night Vision
description: A clean, achievement safe resource pack that makes ores instantly visible with a night-vision style effect in all graphics modes.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: X RAY + Night Vision shows you every ore without disabling achievements. No mods, no commands, just a lightweight resource pack that hides the terrain around ores so they stand out in any graphics mode, and makes them glow when Vibrant Visuals is on. Two X-Ray Modes Pick one in the pack settings (the gear icon on the pack): - X RAY DEFAULT: hides stone, deepslate, tuff, granite, diorite, andesite, dirt, sand, sandstone, plain terracotta, netherrack, basalt, blackstone and other common terrain. Water and lava stay visible, and gravel, obsidian, sculk shriekers and sculk catalysts show as thin markers so you still know where they are. - X RAY 100%: full see-through. On top of the usual terrain it also hides grass blocks, cobblestone, coloured terracotta, snow, ice, nether bricks, nylium, end stone, sculk, dripstone, bone blocks, suspicious sand and gravel, and even water and lava . Spot gravel before it gets you. In X RAY DEFAULT, gravel is drawn as a thin torch-shaped marker instead of a full block, so you can see exactly where it is and avoid digging under it. It's still real gravel and can still fall, the pack only changes how it looks. In X RAY 100% gravel is hidden completely, so take extra care there. See lava before you dig into it. In X RAY DEFAULT, lava stays visible while the stone around it disappears, so hidden lava pools show up clearly while you mine. X RAY 100% hides water and lava too, so switch to DEFAULT when you're mining near lava. Key Features -Ores visible in every graphics mode (Simple, Fancy or Vibrant Visuals) -Two modes, DEFAULT and 100%, switchable any time in pack settings -Ores glow with real PBR texture sets when Vibrant Visuals is on, plus brighter lighting for a night-vision feel -Fog pushed far out in every biome, the Nether and the End -Chests and shulker boxes in bright solid colours so loot stands out -No pumpkin overlay, no falling leaf particles, minimal block-breaking cracks -100% resource pack, achievement-safe and safe to add to existing worlds Recommended Settings -Turn off Smooth Lighting for the clearest ore visibility -Simple or Fancy both work. On Fancy, use the water trick above -Enable Vibrant Visuals for glowing ores (optional but looks amazing) Install Place the resource pack in your resource_packs folder or import it in-game Edit or create a world → Resource Packs → enable X RAY + Night Vision Click the gear icon on the pack to choose X RAY DEFAULT or X RAY 100% Turn off Smooth Lighting for best results Enjoy finding every ore effortlessly!

title: Borderful Glowing Ores
description: Make your caves shine! Glowing ores with realistic emissive lighting for better cave exploration.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: Borderful Glowing Ores Caves are dark, and finding ore usually means burning through a stack of torches just to see what you're swinging at. This pack fixes that. With Vibrant Visuals on, every ore glows with its own emissive light. Diamond shines pale blue from across a ravine, redstone burns red in the dark, and gold catches your eye the moment you round a corner. No behaviour pack, no commands, no lag. ⛏ Two Styles, One Pack Default Glowing Ores The subtle option. Only the ore itself glows, exactly where the mineral sits in the stone. Nothing is outlined, so it just looks like the ore is lit. Best if you want realism and don't want your world to look modded. Borderful Glowing Ores The visibility option. Every ore block gets a coloured, glowing border on top of the glowing ore, so it reads instantly at a distance and in dim light. Great for resource gathering, speedrunning, or anyone who mines with brightness turned down. Swap between the two styles any time in the pack settings, no reinstall needed. 🧩 Compatibility It's 100% resource pack, with no behaviour pack, so achievements stay enabled and it's safe to add to an existing world. It works alongside shaders, PVP packs and other resource packs. Just keep Borderful Glowing Ores above them so its ore textures win. ✅ Compatible with Actions & Stuff Tested with Actions & Stuff by Oreville Studios, and both packs work together. Put Borderful Glowing Ores above Actions & Stuff in your active pack list and the glow works as normal. 🌟 What's Covered Every ore in the game Coal, copper, iron, gold, diamond, emerald, lapis and redstone, plus all their deepslate versions, nether gold ore, nether quartz ore and ancient debris. Beyond ore Amethyst clusters and all three bud stages, the amethyst on calibrated sculk sensors, and cauldron water all get emissive maps too, so geodes light up the same way your mineshaft does. Coloured block light The pack also sets custom light colours for over 100 light-emitting blocks in Vibrant Visuals: torches, soul torches, lanterns, copper torches and lanterns, campfires, candles in every colour, froglights, glowstone, sea lanterns, lava, lit redstone ore and more. Real PBR texture sets These are proper PBR texture sets with tuned emissive and height maps, not brightened colour textures. The glow works with Minecraft's lighting instead of looking like a flat sticker pasted on the wall. Turn The Glow On This is the one step people miss. The glow comes from Minecraft's PBR pipeline, so it only shows up when Vibrant Visuals is active: ➤ Settings → Video → Graphics Mode → Vibrant Visuals (or Ray Tracing, on supported devices) ➤ Move Borderful Glowing Ores to the top of your active resource pack list ➤ Requires Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.80 or newer If your ores look completely normal, it's almost always because Vibrant Visuals is still off. Flip that switch and they'll light up immediately. 🚀 Performance The pack adds no entities and no scripts. It only swaps texture and lighting data, so on its own it costs essentially zero FPS. Vibrant Visuals is the demanding part, and that's Minecraft's renderer, not this pack. If your device runs Vibrant Visuals, it runs Borderful Glowing Ores. 💖 Support Over half a million downloads, thank you! If this pack made your caves better, a rating or a comment really helps, and it's what keeps the updates coming. Found a bug or want an ore handled differently? Leave a comment and I'll take a look. Light up your caves, spot the good stuff from across the room, and stop wasting torches. Happy mining!

title: Clear And Borderless Glass
description: GlowCraft is a stunning Vibrant Visuals shader pack for Minecraft Bedrock that makes blocks, items, particles, & entities glow, bringing true illumination and best visuals to your game.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: Clear & Borderless Glass for Minecraft Bedrock 1.26 — three tiny packs that fix ugly glass Glass is one of the best building blocks in Minecraft — right up until you actually look through it. In vanilla Bedrock every glass block carries a thick, opaque frame, so a wall of glass ends up looking like a spreadsheet instead of a window. Clear & Borderless Glass is a set of three standalone resource packs that remove that frame, keep the transparency, and let your builds finally look the way you imagined them. No subpacks, no settings, no behaviour pack, no experimental toggles. You pick one file, you tap it, and your glass changes. The problem with vanilla glass Open any modern house build and look through the windows. What you see is not the view — it is a grid of white borders stacked on top of the view. Two things make it worse: The frame is per block, not per pane. A 6×4 window is 24 blocks, so you get 24 frames instead of one window frame. The frame is fully opaque , so it survives any lighting, any shader and any angle. That is fine when glass is decoration. It is painful when the glass is the point of the build: aquariums, greenhouses, sky bridges, ocean monuments, modern villas, observation decks, mob farms with glass walls. The three variants Pack File Look Best for Borderless Glass release/borderless-glass.mcpack The frame is gone; only four small corner dots remain Big window walls, aquariums, greenhouses Clear Glass release/clear-glass.mcpack Fully transparent centre with a thin, visible frame Builds where glass must still read as glass Clear & Borderless Glass release/clear-borderless-glass.mcpack Transparent centre and no frame at all The cleanest look — glass that disappears All three cover the same 35 textures, so nothing is missing when you switch: plain glass tinted_glass all 16 stained glass colours the matching 16 glass_pane_top textures (the pane face) Because the packs are three separate files with three different UUIDs, you can install all of them at the same time and activate a different one per world without any conflict. How to install Download the .mcpack you want. Open the file — Minecraft Bedrock launches and imports the pack automatically. Open your world → Settings → Resource Packs → activate the pack. Done. There is no subpack menu and nothing else to configure. It is a pure resource pack: it never touches your world data, so it is safe to add to and remove from an existing survival world, and it works on Realms and servers (client side). Performance Textures are the original 16×16 resolution, so the packs weigh ~90 KB each and cost nothing in FPS — they are the same size files the game already loads, just redrawn. Requirements Minecraft Bedrock 1.26.0 or newer ( min_engine_version: [1, 26, 0] ). No experimental toggles, no Beta APIs, no behaviour pack. Works on Windows, Android, iOS, Xbox, PlayStation and Switch. Asset Path Master video (1:41, 1920×1080) video/clear-borderless-glass-full-video.mp4 Shorts (30s / 29s / 43s, 1080×1920) video/shorts/*.mp4 Thumbnails media/thumbnails/ Pack icons (256×256) source/icons/ Subtitles (AR + EN) video/subtitles-*.srt , video/shorts/*-ar.srt , *-en.srt Frequently asked questions Do I need all three? No. Install the one you like; install all three if you want to switch per world. Can I use it with other resource packs? Yes — put this pack above packs that also touch glass, or below packs that should win. Is it allowed on Realms / servers? Yes. It is client-side only; nobody else has to install it to see their own glass, and it changes no gameplay. (C) Youseef-Tools & IgnisMod

fullDescription: About Glowing Ores makes resource gathering in Minecraft Bedrock easier and more satisfying. Ores stand out on every device: brightened textures on classic graphics, and genuine glow in the dark with Vibrant Visuals. Features Works on every graphics mode : Classic (Simple/Fancy) : ore pixels are brightened and saturated, so veins stand out clearly even in dark caves. Vibrant Visuals : ore veins literally glow in the dark. The glow is graded by each ore's natural shading — crystal facets and metal flecks shine brightest — for a natural, non-flat look. Materials are layered on top of Minecraft's official Vibrant Visuals maps, so metals keep their shine, gems stay glossy, and amethyst keeps its translucency. Activate the Glowing Ores resource pack for your world. Put it at the top of your active resources list to override default textures correctly. (Optional) Turn on Vibrant Visuals in your Video settings to see the ores glow in the dark. Notes This pack does not contain "X-ray" features; it only enhances blocks you are already looking at. The actual glow-in-the-dark effect requires Vibrant Visuals. On classic graphics the brightened textures make ores highly visible but do not emit light. fullDescription: About Invisible Item Frames is a visual resource pack that completely hides standard and glow item frames, making items inside them look as if they are floating in the air. Perfect for builders, clean storage rooms, decorations, and showcase setups. It is client-side, lightweight, and can be activated through Global Resources for use in worlds, servers, and Realms. Features Full Transparency: Makes the wooden border and the background backing of item frames completely invisible. Multiple Modes (Subpacks): Choose which frames you want to hide via settings: Invisible Both: Both standard and glow item frames are invisible. Standard Only: Hides only standard item frames; glow item frames remain visible. Glow Only: Hides only glow item frames; standard item frames remain visible. Pure Resource Pack: No behavior packs, no scripts, no experimental toggles, and no cheats required. Global Resources: Apply the pack client-side without installing a behavior pack on the server or Realm. Other resource packs that change item frames may override it. Vibrant Visuals Compatibility: Keeps Vibrant Visuals available when the pack is enabled on supported devices. How to use Download and open the .mcaddon file to import it into Minecraft Bedrock. In the game settings, go to Global Resources (or your world settings) and activate Invisible Item Frames . The pack name is translated when using Russian or Spanish. Click the gear icon on the active pack to select your preferred mode (Both, Standard Only, or Glow Only). Restart the game client to apply the block configurations. Notes This pack only affects the rendering of the frame itself; items placed inside remain fully visible and render normally. If you change the subpack mode, a full game restart is recommended to refresh the cache. If frames remain visible, check for other resource packs that change item frames and give this pack higher priority where possible. Requirements Minecraft Bedrock Edition 1.26.50 or newer Vibrant Visuals is optional and requires a supported device.

fullDescription: Say goodbye to lag and enjoy smooth, high-FPS gameplay with Ultimate FPS Booster . Leaving distant trees and hills as faint silhouettes. The fog takes on the colour of the sky: soft blue by day, deep navy at dusk, near-black at night. Rain turns it a cold grey. Fog also thickens dynamically ! The fog covers the whole sky, so the horizon disappears. The sun and moon show only as faint glows. You can turn this off to get the open sky back. Water - Water is solid blue; you cannot see below the surface of the water. Every biome has its own water tint. Foliage - Grass & leaves get a punchy, saturated green from the beta version of mc. VFX (Screen Effects) - There are 3: vignette (the screen edges fade into darkness), film grain (flickering noise, sorta like an old camcorder), & chromatic aberration (a coloured lens fringe around the edges of your vision)! Shadows - Shade is a bit deeper, nights are completely dark, and caves are pitch black until you light a torch. Torches also emit a coloured light, not just one fixed color. Sunlight casts blocky, pixelated shadows. Sun & Moon Brightness - The sun and moon are brighter, as in the original shader. You'll see this best with the sky overlay turned off Requirements This pack is best with Vibrant Visuals , though Fancy graphics also suffices! Requires Minecraft: Bedrock v1.26.0 or newer. Vibrant Visuals' Hardware Requirements: Windows : Graphics cards and drivers supporting DirectX 12 Intel GPUs: Intel graphics driver version 31.0.101.3430 or later is required Android: Android devices running on Adreno 640 (something likke Snapdragon 855), Mali-G68 / Mali-G77 (Valhall architecture, like MediaTek 1000 series), Maleoon , PowerVR A-Series , or Xclipse 530 or higher IOS/iPadOS: An iPhone or iPad running on an A12 Bionic , M1 chip , or higher (like teh iPhone XR, iPhone SE 2nd gen, and newer) Customising Somber Slider option What it does Screen Effects: Off Removes the vignette, grain & lens fringe for a clean image Vignette: Off Removes the dark screen edges Chromatic Aberration: Off Removes the coloured lens fringe Noise: Off Removes the film grain Old Foliage Vibrance: Off Puts grass and leaves back to normal Minecraft colours Water Transparency: On Makes water see-through again Fog Sky Overlay: Off Clears the sky so you can see the sun, moon and stars Fog: Off Removes the Somber fog completely Fog Strength: Light Thinner fog that lets you see a lot further Fog Strength: Heavy Thicker, more clautrophobic fog Preset: Subtle A gentler version of everything Preset: Intense Stronger vingette, grain, fog and greener foliage Preset: Nightmare Everything at maximum, with fog closing in within about 10 blocks 👻 Somber (Default) The original Somber look Dependencies This pack looks amazing if paired with the Classic Textures resource pack for Minecraft: Bedrock. Just make sure Somber is at the very bottom of your enabled packs in your world pack settings/global resource settings; otherwise, it won't look very good. Here is the link to the dependency. compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: oSkullo's CPS Counter Keep track of your attack speed and combat performance in real-time. This resource pack adds a clean, customizable CPS counter directly to your HUD, powered entirely by the modern Bedrock UI settings array. You can adjust exactly how the counter looks and where it sits on your screen without ever leaving the game. The Honest Truth: How It Works Due to the technical limitations of the Minecraft Bedrock UI engine, it is impossible to read raw hardware inputs (mouse clicks or screen taps) directly. Because of this, this pack functions as a Hand-Swing Counter. It detects the left-click attacks landed in the last real second based on your character's arm animation. What this means: It is highly accurate for normal gameplay, PvP, and standard clicking. However, if you are drag-clicking or using macros at extreme speeds (20+ CPS), the counter will not maintain a 1:1 ratio with your hardware because the in-game swing animation simply cannot keep up with those speeds. Features & In-Game Customization Taking advantage of the settings array for Minecraft 1.21.0+, you have full control over the HUD element directly from the pack settings: Visibility Controls: Toggle the entire counter on or off, or choose to hide the "CPS" text label to just show the raw numbers. Positioning: Freely move the counter anywhere on your screen using the X (Left/Right) and Y (Up/Down) offset sliders. Scaling: Adjust the size of the counter from a subtle 25% up to a massive 300%. Background Settings: Toggle the dark background on or off, and fine-tune its opacity (0% to 100%) to ensure it never blocks your crosshair visibility. Compatibility Fully compatible with mobile, PC, and console. Created by oSkullo YouTube: oSkullo Discord: discord.gg/oSkullo

fullDescription: BaKu Shader is a lightweight, fully custom atmosphere pack built to make vanilla Minecraft feel cinematic — without touching your FPS the way heavy shader mods do. Every biome in the Overworld, along with the Nether and its sub-biomes, has been given its own custom fog colour, density, and mood, so travelling across the map actually feels like moving through different worlds. What's changed: 🌲 Forests & Woodlands — Deep, saturated greens with a soft golden haze drifting between the trees. Birch, oak, and jungle canopies now carry richer, more natural colour gradients instead of the flat vanilla tint. 🌊 Oceans & Rivers — Warm oceans get a tropical teal glow, cold oceans shift to a steel-blue chill, and rivers stay crisp and clear. Underwater visibility and fog density were tuned separately so caves and open water never feel the same. 💎 Lush & Dripstone Caves — This is where the pack really shines. Lush Caves now carry a glowing cyan-teal mist that makes glow berries and moss pop, while Dripstone Caves get a warm, dusty amber haze for that deep-underground feeling. 🌸 Cherry Grove — A soft, dreamy pink fog blankets the whole biome, making every petal drop feel like a scene out of an anime. 🔥 Nether — Reworked fog across Crimson Forest, Warped Forest, Soulsand Valley, and Basalt Deltas, each with its own distinct colour identity instead of one flat red haze over everything. The main Nether wastes now glow with a deeper, more intense ember tone. ☀️ Sky, Sun & Moon — Brand new sun texture with a soft bloom and light-ray glow for those golden-hour moments, plus a completely hand-crafted 8-phase moon (yes, all 8 phases actually look correct in-game, not just recoloured circles). Clouds and weather (rain/snow) textures were also refreshed for a softer, less "blocky" look. 🎨 Colour Grading — New grass, foliage, and birch colour maps give the whole world a slightly richer, more vibrant palette without looking unnatural or over-saturated. Performance: Since this pack works entirely through vanilla fog and colour systems (no custom shader code), it runs on any device that supports resource packs — phones, tablets, consoles, and low-end PCs included. No RTX or "Vibrant Visuals" support required. Compatible with: Survival, Creative, Realms, and most other resource/texture packs (it only touches fog, sky, and colour maps — no block textures are overridden, so it stacks cleanly with your favourite texture pack). Installation: Download the .mcpack file Tap it to auto-import into Minecraft Go to your World Settings → Resource Packs → activate BK Shader Move it to the top of your active pack list if you're using it with another texture pack This is a fully original pack — every fog setting, texture, and colour map was built from scratch for this release. No assets were copied from any other shader or resource pack. Got feedback or a biome that still doesn't feel right? Drop a comment — updates are planned based on community feedback. 🎨 Credits Created by: Baku_Studio Pack: BaKu Shader Type: Fog / Atmosphere / Colour-grading Resource Pack (no custom textures overridden) Engine version: 1.20.0+ License: Free to use and share. title: GURJAR X Noir Shader
description: GURJAR X Noir Shader transforms Minecraft Bedrock into a dramatic black-and-white world — deep contrast, moody shadows and cinematic monochrome lighting inspired by classic film noir.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: GURJAR X Noir Shader is a lightweight, single-style visual pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition, built on Mojang's native Vibrant Visuals render pipeline. Where every other filter in this series leans into color — Vivid's saturation, Cartoon's punch, Retro's warmth — Noir strips it all away and goes in the opposite direction entirely: a bold, dramatic, almost entirely monochrome world built around light, shadow, and contrast rather than hue. Color Grading — This is the heart of the Noir identity. Saturation is pushed down to nearly zero across shadows, midtones, and highlights alike, stripping color out of the entire scene and leaving behind a true black-and-white presentation. But this isn't a flat grayscale filter slapped over the top — contrast and gamma are carefully tuned so that blacks stay deep and rich, whites stay bright and clean, and the full tonal range in between remains readable and detailed, exactly like classic film noir cinematography. The result feels less like a color image with the saturation turned down and more like the game was shot on black-and-white film from the start. Lighting — Noir leans hard into dramatic, high-contrast lighting. Rather than smooth, even illumination, the sun's brightness and positioning are tuned to create striking pools of light against darker surroundings — long shadows, bright highlights, and a strong sense of directionality. This is what gives Noir its "dramatic lighting" character: scenes feel staged and cinematic, with light doing as much storytelling as the landscape itself. Atmospherics — Sky scattering is tuned to support the monochrome mood — soft, moody, and atmospheric rather than colorful, so skies read as bright fog-like gradients of light and dark instead of blue expanses. This keeps the focus on shape, silhouette, and contrast, the classic visual language of noir film. Shadows — Noir uses more defined, higher-contrast shadow rendering than the softer filters in this series, reinforcing the dramatic, high-contrast aesthetic. Shadows aren't just present — they're part of the composition, adding depth and mood to builds, caves, and forests alike. Water — Even without color, water keeps its natural wave motion and caustic detailing, appearing as shimmering light and dark patterns rather than colored ripples, fitting naturally into the monochrome world without looking flat or lifeless. Because this pack uses a proper dedicated subpack structure (rather than a root-only setup), it loads reliably and automatically the moment it's enabled — no slider, no filter menu, no risk of silent failure. Enable it, and the Noir look is active immediately, every time you load into a world. Noir works especially well for atmospheric builds, horror maps, detective/mystery-themed servers, black-and-white photography-style screenshots, or simply for players who want to experience familiar terrain in a completely new, moody light. Requirements: Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.80+, with the Vibrant Visuals experimental toggle enabled at world creation, on a device capable of running the deferred rendering pipeline. Install: Tap the .mcpack file to import it into Minecraft, then activate only this pack under Resource Packs before creating or loading a world. If you've previously installed Cinematic, Vivid, Retro, Cartoon, or Standard from this series, make sure they are disabled or removed first — only one shader-style pack should be active at a time. 🙌 Credits - GURJAR

fullDescription: GURJAR X Standard Shader is a lightweight, single-style visual pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition, built on Mojang's native Vibrant Visuals render pipeline. Unlike the more stylized entries in this shader family — Cinematic's dramatic golden-hour mood, Vivid's punchy saturation, Retro's nostalgic amber haze, or Cartoon's bold comic-book pop — Standard is built around one core idea: give the game a clean, natural, dependable look that works well no matter what you're doing. Whether you're building, exploring, farming, fighting mobs, or just relaxing and taking in the scenery, Standard keeps the world looking believable and pleasant without pulling focus with heavy stylization. Lighting — The sun and moon follow a smooth, realistic illuminance and color curve across the full day-night cycle. Unlike Cinematic's dramatic golden-hour spikes or Retro's constant warm haze, Standard's lighting transitions gently — mornings feel fresh, midday feels bright and clear, and evenings shift naturally into warmer tones without ever feeling exaggerated. This makes long play sessions comfortable on the eyes and keeps builds, terrain, and mobs looking true to their intended colors at any time of day. Atmospherics — Sky scattering and horizon blending are tuned for a natural, believable sky — blue during the day, softly warming near sunrise and sunset, with light, realistic fog rather than heavy stylized haze. Distant terrain stays visible and readable, which is especially useful for builders and explorers who need to judge distances and landmarks accurately rather than fight against an overly dramatic atmosphere. Color Grading — Where the other filters push saturation, contrast, or warmth hard in one direction, Standard keeps color grading balanced: mild, natural saturation, gentle contrast, and a neutral tone-mapping curve. Grass looks green, stone looks grey, water looks blue — nothing is exaggerated or tinted for artistic effect. This makes Standard an excellent all-purpose base, especially for players who want Vibrant Visuals' improved lighting engine without a strong artistic "filter" changing how their builds and textures actually look. Shadows — Soft-filtered shadows with natural falloff keep the world grounded and three-dimensional without harsh, distracting edges, matching the overall calm, dependable character of this style. Water — Natural wave motion, subtle wind-driven ripples, and a standard caustics texture keep oceans, rivers, and lakes looking alive and realistic, without the exaggerated shimmer or stylized tint found in some of the other filters. Because this pack uses a single dedicated subpack (rather than a root-only setup), it loads reliably and automatically the moment it's enabled — there's no slider to fiddle with, no filter menu to navigate, and no risk of it silently failing to apply. Enable the pack, and the Standard look is active immediately, every time. Requirements: Minecraft Bedrock 1.21.80+, with the Vibrant Visuals experimental toggle enabled at world creation, on a device capable of running the deferred rendering pipeline. Install: Tap the .mcpack file to import it into Minecraft, then activate only this pack under Resource Packs before creating or loading a world. If you've previously installed Cinematic, Vivid, Retro, or Cartoon from this same series, make sure they are disabled or removed first — only one shader-style pack should be active at a time, since they share the same internal structure and the top-most active pack will always take priority. 🙌 Credits- GURJAR

fullDescription: YG Dreamy Shader is a hand-tuned Vibrant Visuals configuration for Minecraft: Bedrock Edition, built to make every biome feel like it's lit from within. Unlike traditional GLSL shader packs for Java Edition, YG Dreamy Shader runs entirely on Mojang's native Vibrant Visuals (RenderDragon) pipeline — no mods, no heavy external renderer, just a resource pack you drop straight into Minecraft. The heart of this pack is light. Sun rays have been sharpened and intensified so that early morning and late evening light cuts dramatically through forest canopies, bamboo groves, and swamp mist, creating those unmistakable "god ray" moments PC shader fans love. The sky itself has been retuned across the full day-night cycle: sunrise and sunset horizons burn with deeper oranges and pinks, the overhead sky reads richer and more saturated, and moonlit nights carry a cool, believable blue glow. Color grading has been pushed further across shadows, midtones, and highlights, giving the whole world a warmer, more vivid, slightly dreamy look without blowing out detail or crushing shadows — thanks to ACES tone mapping doing the heavy lifting under the hood. Water reflects and catches caustic light more noticeably, glowing blocks like torches, lanterns, glowstone, shroomlight, and portals burn brighter, and volumetric fog has been thickened just enough to make light shafts genuinely visible without fogging up your view distance. The Nether and The End get special attention. Crimson Forest, Warped Forest, Basalt Deltas, Soul Sand Valley, and the classic Nether wastes each carry their own boosted, neon-leaning color identity, while the End's purple skies and glowing towers are pushed into full, saturated glow — matching the moody, otherworldly look that inspired this edit. Every biome in the game is covered, from oceans and mesas to cherry groves and the pale garden, each with its own fine-tuned atmosphere, fog, and color grading file, so the pack behaves consistently no matter where you explore. It ships with two cloud options — vanilla clouds for lower-end devices, and a custom 32x cloud subpack for a softer, more painterly sky on stronger hardware. YG Dreamy Shader is best experienced on devices that support Vibrant Visuals (Minecraft 1.21.120+, with PBR/RenderDragon graphics enabled). It's built for players who want their Bedrock world to feel cinematic — warm sunsets, glowing biomes, and rays of light you can actually see — without installing a single shader mod. fullDescription: Step into a world reimagined. YG Fantasy Shader is a vibrant, glow-forward visual overhaul for Minecraft Bedrock Edition, built on the RenderDragon Vibrant Visuals lighting engine and crafted to turn every sunrise, sunset, and starlit night into a cinematic fantasy scene. At the heart of this shader is light itself. The sun no longer just rises, it blazes. Enhanced Mie scattering wraps the horizon in bold, sweeping sun rays, while a broadened golden-hour glow bathes the land in warm amber and rose-gold tones before the sky dissolves into deep violet twilight. Rayleigh scattering has been pushed further, giving the sky a richer, more saturated gradient that shifts from soft blue daylight into dramatic magenta and purple sunsets reminiscent of a painted fantasy realm. Beneath that sky, volumetric fog does more than add distance haze, it catches the light. Increased scattering density and tightened forward scattering make crepuscular light shafts punch through forest canopies and cave openings, giving every biome a sense of atmosphere and depth that vanilla lighting simply cannot match. Underground, the world glows back. Every ore, diamond, emerald, gold, redstone, lapis, copper, and their deepslate variants, has had its emissive properties intensified, so veins genuinely shine in caves rather than sitting flat and dull. Combined with subtly boosted PBR emissive fallback values across blocks, items, actors, and particles, the whole world carries a faint, living luminescence, from lanterns and campfires to enchanted structures. Color grading ties it all together with a refined highlights-midtones-shadows pipeline, boosted saturation and gain, and ACES tone mapping for a cinematic, high-dynamic-range look that avoids blown-out whites or muddy shadows. A tuned white balance keeps warm light feeling warm and cool night skies feeling appropriately cool. Despite all these enhancements, YG Fantasy Shader is built to stay performance-friendly. It uses Minecraft Bedrock's native Vibrant Visuals configuration system rather than heavy custom shader code, meaning it runs efficiently on a wide range of devices, including many mobile and console setups, without the frame-rate cost of traditional shader packs. Whether you're exploring a lush jungle at dawn, mining through glowing deepslate caverns, or watching a violet aurora roll over the night sky above your base, YG Fantasy Shader is designed to make every moment in your world feel like a page out of an epic fantasy story. Grab your torch, watch the horizon catch fire at dawn, and see Minecraft Bedrock the way it was always meant to glow. title: Golden Glow Shader
description: A warm, cinematic golden-hour reskin for Vibrant Visuals — glowing low sun, soft amber haze, filmic color grading, and tannin-warm water across 47 biomes, with a rose-gold variant for Cherry Grove.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: Golden Glow Shader reskins Minecraft Bedrock's Vibrant Visuals renderer for a warm, cinematic look inspired by golden-hour photography. Instead of a compiled shader binary, it is built entirely from Mojang's official Vibrant Visuals JSON systems: lighting, atmospherics, color grading and water. That keeps it lightweight and transparent, and compatible with every device Vibrant Visuals already runs on, from phones to consoles to PC, with no extra performance cost beyond Vibrant Visuals itself. The sunrise and sunset window is stretched and deepened, with the sun's color sliding through warm gold and amber instead of snapping straight from white to dark. Mie scattering around the sun is boosted for a soft, glowing halo, while the sky blends from a warm cream horizon into a deep dusk zenith overhead. Color grading pushes orange-leaning highlights against slightly cooler shadows for a filmic split-tone, finished with ACES tonemapping, lifted saturation, and a warm 5200K color temperature that ties the whole scene together. Water gets gentle tannin warmth, visible caustics, and softened waves, so lakes, rivers and oceans glow instead of looking flat and blue. Rather than one global override, these settings are applied individually across 47 overworld biomes, so plains, forests, jungles, deserts, oceans, swamps and snowy biomes each get an appropriate variant — swamps run murkier and greener, open water stays clearer and tealer, deserts and savannas lean into the warmth naturally. Cherry Grove breaks from the orange palette entirely for its own rose-and-gold variant, matching its pink blossoms instead of fighting them. Requirements: Minecraft Bedrock 1.26.40 or newer, with the "Vibrant Visuals" experimental toggle switched on in world settings. No other experiments, add-ons, or behavior packs are needed — just enable Vibrant Visuals and apply the pack. Created by GURJAR. Credits Author / Creator: GURJAR Built with: Minecraft Bedrock's official Vibrant Visuals JSON API (lighting, atmospherics, color grading, water, client biomes) — no third-party shader code or compiled binaries included. Engine target: Minecraft Bedrock 1.26.40+ Key Features Extended, deepened golden-hour sun with a soft glowing halo Warm horizon-to-zenith sky gradient Filmic color grading (orange highlights / cool shadows) with ACES tonemapping Tannin-warm, clearer water with visible caustics and softened waves Per-biome tuning across 47 overworld biomes (not one flat global look) Unique rose-gold variant for Cherry Grove Pure JSON — no compiled shader binaries, small download size Requirements Minecraft Bedrock Edition 1.26.40 or newer Vibrant Visuals experimental toggle enabled in world settings No other experiments or add-ons required Installation Download and open `GoldenGlowShader_by_GURJAR_v0.1.1.mcpack` — Minecraft will import it automatically. Create or edit a world → Settings → Experiments → enable Vibrant Visuals. Go to Resource Packs, find Golden Glow Shader under My Packs, and activate it. Play — the effect is visible immediately, strongest around in-game sunrise/sunset.

fullDescription: My Music Player 1.4 — Update Notes Important: Song Naming System Changed If you downloaded an older version of My Music Player, your existing song filenames may not work with this version. The current version uses numbered song names. Rename your music files to 1, 2, 3, 4.... Song Naming Format Each song must use its corresponding number: Song 1 → 1.ogg Song 2 → 2.ogg Song 3 → 3.ogg Song 4 → 4.ogg Song 5 → 5.ogg Continue the same numbering system for the rest of your songs, up to Song 100. My Music Player is a resource pack for Minecraft Bedrock Edition that adds a simple in-game music player. Unlike normal music packs, this pack does not include any songs. This keeps the download small and avoids copyright issues. Instead, you can add your own music to the pack. Features: In-game music player menu Supports multiple custom songs Works in Minecraft Bedrock Edition Lightweight resource pack *No Copyrighed Music Included How to add your own music: Download and install the resource pack. Open the pack's music folder (MyMusicPlayer/sounds/music/). Convert your music to .OGG format. Copy the files into the music folder. Rename them like this: song_1.ogg song_2.ogg song_3.ogg song_4.ogg ... Enable the resource pack and open the in-game Music Player menu. Press the button for the song you want to play. *Important No music is included with this pack. You must provide your own audio files. Only use music that you own or have permission to use. Songs must be in .OGG format and follow the correct file names (song_1, song_2, song_3, etc.), otherwise they won't play. Enjoy your favorite music while exploring your Minecraft worlds! 🎶 FAQs Q: Why isn't there a Stop Music button? A: A true Stop Music button isn't currently possible using only a Minecraft Bedrock resource pack. While an addon could provide more control, it would reduce compatibility with servers and Realms, make installation more complex, and may cause issues if removed from a world. My Music Player is designed to work as a standalone resource pack with maximum compatibility. Q: Can other players hear the music I play? A: No. My Music Player is a client-side resource pack, so the music only plays for you. Other players in your world or server cannot hear it.

title: The Forgotten Winter
description: The Forgotten Winter transforms Minecraft into a frozen world of the past. Lush greenery becomes snow-covered, frosted foliage, icy plants and wintry landscapes, while subtle mob and environmental changes bring an Ice Age atmosphere to the Overworld.
compatibility: Bedrock向け（配布元でバージョン確認）
fullDescription: The Forgotten Winter transforms Minecraft into a frozen world of the past. Lush greenery becomes snow-covered, frosted foliage, icy plants, and wintry landscapes, while subtle mob and environmental changes bring an Ice Age atmosphere to the Overworld. The pack goes far beyond simple texture changes, introducing custom models, particles, sounds, fog, colormaps, and environmental effects throughout the world. Animals and hostile mobs take on cold-weather appearances, deserts become barren frozen landscapes, and features like ice crystals, falling snow, winter birds, falling branches, and ground ice add life and detail to the environment. At the center of the transformation is a fully remodeled mammoth, replacing the camel while retaining its original animations and rideability. Snowstorms replace rain, snow visually accumulates around the player, and over 80 biomes receive a colder, frostier atmosphere. Despite the scale of the transformation, everything is achieved through a resource pack without changing gameplay or behavior, preserving Minecraft's original mechanics while making the Overworld feel like a world forgotten to time. Screenshots List of Features Features Mob Changes Camel → Mammoth — A fully remodeled mammoth using the camel's animations and remaining rideable. Cold Animals — Chickens, cows, and pigs permanently use their cold-weather variants. Snowy Villagers — Villagers always wear their snow-biome clothing. Frozen Mobs — Creepers, skeletons, spiders, zombies, husks, drowned, and iron golems receive custom snowy/cold textures. Vegetation Snow-Covered Foliage — All leaves (except cherry and birch) , grasses, ferns, vines, firefly bushes, and normal bushes receive handcrafted snowy-white textures. White Vegetation Colormap — All vegetation uses a custom white winter colormap. Dead Birch Trees — Birch leaves are replaced with dark, empty foliage to create the appearance of dead trees. Winter Flowers — Flowers receive darker green stems, with snowy variants for poppies and dandelions. Snowy Crops — Fully grown crops receive custom snow-covered textures. Blocks & Terrain Snowy Grass Blocks — Regular grass blocks are replaced with snow-covered grass blocks. Snow-Covered Crops & Produce — Hay bales, melons, and pumpkins receive new snow-covered textures. Frozen Dripstone — Dripstone is redesigned as 3D ice crystals with a custom model and ice texture. Ground Ice — Thin ice sheets form across the ground during snowfall. Desert Overhaul Cold Grey Sands — Deserts are transformed with pale, cold-grey sand. Scattered Bones — Short dry grass becomes scattered bones with a custom model and texture. Dead Vegetation — Tall dry grass and dead bushes receive varied dark-brown dead vegetation textures. Dead Cacti — Cacti are redesigned with spruce-log textures and custom cactus flowers, while spruce-leaf elements create the appearance of nearly leafless trees. Ground Details Ice Crystals — Leaf litter is replaced by scattered ice crystals in forests. Custom 3D model Multiple varied textures Custom sound New in-game name: Ice Crystals Custom item texture Weather & Atmosphere Snowstorms — Rain is replaced with custom snowstorms and snow particles. Snow Accumulation — Snow visually accumulates on blocks around the player during storms. (Separate from vanilla snow layers and purely visual.) Frosty Fog — Over 80 biomes receive denser, colder-looking fog. Storm Fog — Fog becomes even denser during snowstorms. Ground Ice Formation — Snowfall can visually create thin ice sheets across the terrain. Particles & Ambient Life Cold Breath — New cold-breath particles for the player. Falling Snow — Custom snow particles replace vanilla rain. Falling Leaves — Every leaf type has custom falling-leaf particles with two snowy variants. Falling Birch Branches — Birch particles use custom textures and physics to resemble falling branches. Winter Birds — Four ambient bird particles spawn around trees: black, white, grey, and light brown. 3D Torch Flame — Torches feature a new crossed 3D flame particle.

fullDescription: Baku Abandoned City Shader Author: Baku_Studio Baku Abandoned City Shader is an original Minecraft Bedrock Edition resource pack built for the official Vibrant Visuals (RenderDragon) graphics mode. It is designed to reproduce a soft, cinematic, atmospheric daylight look with natural lighting, gentle fog, muted greens and calm teal water while fully preserving Minecraft’s classic block style and pixel textures. Pack Information Pack Name: Baku Abandoned City Shader Author: Baku_Studio Type: Vibrant Visuals / PBR Resource Pack Supported Versions: Minecraft Bedrock Edition & Pocket Edition 1.21.120 and newer (1.21 – 1.26 generation) Required Graphics Mode: Vibrant Visuals Platform: Android, iOS, Windows, Xbox, PlayStation (devices that support Vibrant Visuals) Installation Import into Minecraft Bedrock. Activate the pack. Set Graphics Mode → Vibrant Visuals . Play. Visual Style The pack focuses on a peaceful, soft, slightly hazy cinematic atmosphere. Lighting is warm-neutral and diffused. Shadows stay soft and never pure black. Distant terrain fades naturally into atmospheric haze. Colors remain muted and natural — especially the greens of grass and leaves. Water appears translucent teal/cyan with soft reflections. The overall mood is calm, immersive and modern while still looking unmistakably like Minecraft. Features Lighting Soft warm-neutral directional sunlight Smooth highlight rolloff (no harsh white clipping) Balanced ambient fill so shadows remain visible Natural contrast between direct sun, ambient light and shade Atmosphere & Fog Soft layered distance fog Atmospheric haze and depth separation Bright horizon glow Mie scattering for gentle sun glow / bloom-like effect Smooth blending of distant terrain into the sky Color Grading Muted cinematic green vegetation Natural medium-to-dark grass and leaf tones Soft shadow lift Controlled highlight compression Subtle warm color temperature (~5800 K) Filmic-style tone mapping Water Translucent teal / cyan-green body color Soft environment and sky reflections Gentle surface waves Soft specular highlights Depth-based coloration Not flat blue and not mirror-like Shadows & Materials Soft natural shadow appearance Subtle ambient occlusion influence through lighting balance Default PBR material response tuned for realistic roughness Preserves original Minecraft block textures and geometry Time of Day Support Keyframed values for sunrise, day, sunset and night Warmer light and stronger haze at sunrise/sunset Cooler ambient tones at night What This Pack Does NOT Do Does not replace Minecraft textures with realistic or AI-upscaled textures Does not change block geometry or proportions Does not require RTX, Java Edition, OptiFine, Iris or any external shader loader Does not use unsupported or invented JSON properties Technical Details Uses only official Vibrant Visuals systems: lighting/global.json atmospherics/atmospherics.json color_grading/color_grading.json water/water.json pbr/global.json Capability: "pbr" Minimum engine version: 1.21.120 Lightweight configuration-only pack (excellent performance) Installation Import the .mcpack file into Minecraft Bedrock. Activate Baku Abandoned City Shader in Global Resources or World Resource Packs. Go to Settings → Video → Graphics Mode and select Vibrant Visuals . Enter any world. Performance The pack is very lightweight because it only adjusts lighting, atmosphere, water and color grading parameters. It runs well on mobile devices that support Vibrant Visuals as well as on Windows and consoles. Credits Created by Baku_Studio . This is an original implementation inspired by cinematic soft-lighting reference visuals. No proprietary shader source code was used or copied.
